title: Manetti Shrem Museum: Together Again, 1960–2026, Perspectives from UC Davis’ Fine Arts Collection
location: Jan Shrem and Maria Manetti Shrem Museum of Art at UC Davis, 254 Old Davis Road, Davis, CA, 95616, United States
description:
Together Again inaugurates the Manetti Shrem Museum’s ongoing collection galleries. This exhibition highlighting the collection will be on long-term view, accompanied by temporary exhibitions each fall and winter. 
The ongoing collection galleries trace a history of art forged from UC Davis and throughout Northern California. By focusing on relationships of many kinds, this presentation proposes that in order to understand an artwork in all its fullness, chance encounters and long-standing friendships often matter as much as formal affiliations. UC Davis legends such as Wayne Thiebaud, Deborah Butterfield and Bruce Nauman are exhibited alongside important regional voices that were once overlooked, and the exhibition extends to the artists shaping Northern California today, including Sadie Barnette, Woody De Othello and Ruby Neri. Together Again builds bridges between who we were and who we are becoming at UC Davis, and affirms the Manetti Shrem Museum as home to the complex story of Northern California art — rich in legacy and always in the process of becoming. 
The collection will be open Wednesdays to Sundays, 10 a.m. to 5 p.m. The location is the Jan Shrem and Maria Manetti Shrem Museum of Art at UC Davis. Admission is free.

title: Portraits of Things: Paintings by Gioia Fonda and Charlie Gill
location: Pence Gallery, 212 D Street, Davis, CA 95616
description:
Portraits of Things: Paintings by Gioia Fonda and Charlie Gill at Pence Gallery in Davis 
Exhibit: October 9 – November 29, 2026 
Reception: Friday, October 9, 6-9 PM (Free) 
Artist Talk: Sunday, November 8, 2-3:30 PM (Free) 
  
Interdisciplinary artist Gioia Fonda has long collected colorful toys, both for their intrinsic charm and as creative inspiration. As a student at California College of the Arts, she arranged small collectibles into still-life compositions, captured them on film, and processed the photos at a local drugstore. Captivated by these arrangements, her advisor, Charlie Gill, painted spare compositions based on her photographs—works that now hang alongside hers. For this exhibition, Fonda has created a series of new paintings featuring similar arrangements of toys and found objects. She is also offering an opportunity for members of the public to exhibit their own small works on paper, riffing on some of her recent photos. Artists may add to this display throughout the duration of the show.  
  
Sponsored by the Pence Community Curatorial Fund. 
  
Image: Gioia Fonda, “Holding It Together”

description:
Live Music @ The Melon Ball in Davis. 
A post-Halloween costume party featuring Bloom Ritual, Roni Jean and Valley Taylor. Costume not required; but best costume wins a 3 band merch package! 
Roni Jean carves out a unique niche with a blend of Haunted Indie Rock, Dreampop, and Shoegaze in Sacramento, CA. Their music weaves lush, dynamic soundscapes with a melodic melancholy that always carries an undeniable edge. Drawing inspiration from artists like Sir Chloe, Wisp, and Radiohead, Roni Jean moves seamlessly between moments of delicate vulnerability and explosive, powerful expression. 
Bloom Ritual; from my rat infested studio to your ears. From an alternative foundation, Bloom Ritual bleeds into adjacent genres such as psychedelic, shoegaze, indie rock and post-hardcore. The latter sound is more easily recognizable in the upcoming EP release, whereas the band’s previously released tracks, such as “Heaven” and “Fish Bowl,” are closely tethered to the ethereal shoegaze genre. It’s psychedelic rock that doesn’t try hard to be psychedelic; it just seems to end up there after all the genres blend together. 
Valley Taylor; Valley Taylor makes songs, drawings, videos and other things in El Cerrito, California. The music moves somewhere between Indie Rock, lo-fi Folk and Ambient Music, usually built from guitars, old sounds, field recordings and whatever else happens to make its way in. Sometimes it becomes a record. Sometimes it becomes a drawing or a little film. Sometimes it just lives on the internet somewhere.

title: 9th Annual Winters Salmon Festival
location: Rotary Park – Winters, 201 Railroad Ave, Winters, CA, 95694
description:
The Winters Salmon Festival is held every year to honor the return of Chinook salmon (also known as King Salmon) to Lower Putah Creek. Salmon return to Putah Creek around October every year in order to spawn. This migration has grown and in recent years we have welcomed over 2,000 salmon! 
This festival celebrates the collaborative effort to restore portions of Putah Creek, which resulted in the arrival of a salmon run. The return of salmon shows the resilience of nature to bounce back when the community comes together to help.  
Join us in welcoming salmon back to Putah Creek with live music, children’s activities, food trucks, and more!

title: I-Fest 2026
location: International House Davis, 10 College Park, Davis, CA, 95616, United States
description:
Join us on November 7 at International House Davis for I-Fest 2026, our International Festival Davis! 
For one day, we open our doors wide to celebrate and uplift the many cultures and people who make our region so vibrant. Explore cultural and artisan booths throughout I-House, enjoy food trucks out front, and experience a full lineup of performances on our backyard stage. It’s an open house in the truest sense: for the day, this is your house too, and every culture and community has a place here. 
I-Fest is a celebration, but your participation also supports the work I-House does all year long: welcoming newcomers, supporting English learners, and helping people from around the world find connection and community in Davis. At a time when many of us are feeling anxious or disconnected, creating spaces for joy, belonging, and connection feels more important than ever. Come celebrate cultures, meet new people, share in the joy, and experience what makes our community so special. 
For one day, I-House is your house. Come be part of it.

title: Let's talk about Female Sexuality & Fluidity
description:
Iama Embodied Community
If you have ever questioned your sexuality, experienced unexpected attraction, fallen for someone who challenged how you understood your sexual identity, or simply wondered why we don’t talk more openly about women’s sexuality, this event is for you.

I thought I was heterosexual until I fell in love with a woman. Reading Sexual Fluidity by Lisa Diamond has helped me make sense of my experience, and it made me realize how many women might be navigating similar questions without having a safe space to talk about them.

Come join us in a frank, open conversation and connect with other women with similar experiences. Let's talk about sexual fluidity and unexpected attraction, questioning or rethinking the labels we’ve used to understand ourselves, dating patterns, desire, and the ways our experiences of attraction may change, sexual shame, social expectations, and the messages we’ve inherited about sexuality, gender, identity, and giving ourselves permission to explore without needing all the answers (and labels), what else is on YOUR mind??

We’ll meet at Betty on T, they have coffee, tea, wine, and food options. Depending on our group size and the weather we’ll find a spot indoors or on the heated patio. I’ll have a sign on our table. Please RSVP to help with the reservation.

If you know a woman who might appreciate this kind of space, please share the event with her. You never know who might be looking for this conversation.

**About the hostess**

I’m Rola (pronounced Ru-lah), I am a pastor, yoga instructor, somatic guide, and trauma-informed facilitator currently working toward becoming a somatic coach. I bring experience in group facilitation, integrative somatic trauma therapy, embodiment, and a deep curiosity about the ways we experience ourselves and relate to one another.

**P.S.**

* This isn’t a formal workshop or a lecture. I’ll bring a few prompts to get the conversation started, but my hope is that it unfolds organically, shaped who shows up and what we feel moved to share
* There is no pressure to disclose anything personal, you are welcome to share, ask questions, or simply listen or be present
* You don’t need to be questioning your sexuality or have a particular identity to join. Even if you’re just curious about female sexuality and how it unfolds, you are welcome
* This space is for female-bodied individuals

title: Manetti Shrem Museum: Together Again, 1960–2026, Perspectives from UC Davis’ Fine Arts Collection
location: Jan Shrem and Maria Manetti Shrem Museum of Art at UC Davis, 254 Old Davis Road, Davis, CA, 95616, United States
description:
Together Again inaugurates the Manetti Shrem Museum’s ongoing collection galleries. This exhibition highlighting the collection will be on long-term view, accompanied by temporary exhibitions each fall and winter. 
The ongoing collection galleries trace a history of art forged from UC Davis and throughout Northern California. By focusing on relationships of many kinds, this presentation proposes that in order to understand an artwork in all its fullness, chance encounters and long-standing friendships often matter as much as formal affiliations. UC Davis legends such as Wayne Thiebaud, Deborah Butterfield and Bruce Nauman are exhibited alongside important regional voices that were once overlooked, and the exhibition extends to the artists shaping Northern California today, including Sadie Barnette, Woody De Othello and Ruby Neri. Together Again builds bridges between who we were and who we are becoming at UC Davis, and affirms the Manetti Shrem Museum as home to the complex story of Northern California art — rich in legacy and always in the process of becoming. 
The collection will be open Wednesdays to Sundays, 10 a.m. to 5 p.m. The location is the Jan Shrem and Maria Manetti Shrem Museum of Art at UC Davis. Admission is free.

Big Joe Kennedy is a New Orleans pianist, bandleader, and performer known for concert experiences that are as musically rich as they are audience-engaging.

He served as pianist with the Dukes of Dixieland from 2013 to 2022, performing for audiences across the country, and remains a fixture at premier New Orleans venues including Mahogany Jazz Hall, The New Orleans Jazz National Historical Park, and The Carousel Lounge. 
His concert program, A Taste of New Orleans, guides audiences through the traditions that shaped American music, from Traditional Jazz to New Orleans R&B, with the authority and warmth of an artist who has spent decades inside this music.

5TH St Gallos – The music curated by the Gallos of the Fifth can be described as an amalgamated sound bringing folk punk vocals through prog heavy bass riffs, riding out jazz metal groves on percussion. 
They hail from the “Dirty 530” aka YOLO County or more reasonably known as Woodland. Through their love of music, art, literature and snuff films these three locals have combined forces to bring a raw, guttural natural energy that leaves audiences in a state of motion. 
Mexican culture is evident in their music as they sing in Spanish at times over punk heavy melodic riffs or dark themes of death and consumption in varied time signatures. 
Fifth Street Gallos were born through ear splitting train whistles waking up members at their “Coop” the infamous band party house on 5th where Roosters, hens and chicks openly roamed the street and sang through the day. 
The Gallos intend to take audiences to the after party reality that is the birth of their sound – Like the birds chirping in the morning and the sun rising, exposing all your flaws while cleansing you of previous woes.

Dark Satellite’s three members grew up playing different styles, coming together to form a one of a kind band with a coalescence of riffs and song structures. Mixing various types of rock genres, blues, jazz and experimental indie progressions, results in their own unique aesthetic and wall of sound. 
Their current album “Splitting Image” was released in August of 2025. As well as written and recorded in about a year and a half in between Dark Satellite’s touring schedule. Every riff, chord and melody that struck an emotional kick with all members was included in this album. “Splitting Image” came to life on its own. Through every set back and downfall they faced as a band they decided to keep pushing, keep booking, and to keep writing. This current album showcases what the band has been through, and the overall direction they are going in, style and attitude wise.

description:
This presentation brings together Catherine Hatzakos, Continuing Lecturer in the Writing Center, and Matthew Conner, Arts, Humanities, and Social Sciences Librarian, to discuss tools, pedagogies, and learning outcomes for teaching about disinformation. Register here 
2026-2027 marks the UC Davis Campus Community Book Project’s 25th anniversary, and our theme—civil liberties—leans into the Book Project’s legacy of promoting dialogue and engaging diverse perspectives and audiences. Our selection, On Tyranny: Twenty Lessons from the Twentieth Century by Timothy Snyder is a call to arms and a guide to resistance, with invaluable ideas for how we can preserve our freedoms in the uncertain years to come. The Founding Fathers tried to protect us from the threat they knew, the tyranny that overcame ancient democracy. Today, our political order faces new threats, not unlike the totalitarianism of the twentieth century. We are no wiser than the Europeans who saw democracy yield to fascism, Nazism, or communism. Our one advantage is that we might learn from their experience. Author Timothy Snyder holds the inaugural Temerty Chair in Modern European History at the Munk School of Global Affairs and Public Policy at the University of Toronto. He is also a permanent fellow at the Institute for Human Sciences in Vienna and the head of the academic advisory council of Ukrainian History Global Initiative. You can read more about the selection here.

title: Davis Farmers Market
location: Central Park, 301 C Street, Davis, CA, 95616, United States
description:
Year-round at Central Park in downtown Davis, thousands gather each week to shop for what is grown, raised, and made locally at our markets. We are dedicated to bringing farmers right to your table, so we stay open rain or shine. 
Walk rows of stalls lined with an array of fruits and vegetables, including certified organic produce, choice meats, chicken, seafood, wine, local eggs and honey. Choose from a variety of fresh-baked goods, plants, flowers and gifts. Enjoy a picnic from one of our many food stands, made from market ingredients.
